topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Genetic Drivers of Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the biological foundation of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by somatic mutations, microenvironmental support, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Epidemiology, and the 'Bad Luck' Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures and lifestyle factors interact with random intrinsic mutations, as demonstrated by public debates and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which infectious agents, chemical carcinogens, metabolic activation, chronic inflammation, and tumor promoters drive malignant transformation across different tissues.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether specific exposures cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides final concluding remarks on weighing carcinogen risks against benefits and closes the lecture.
